quant: oQ4e (4-bit affine group-64; 8-bit on attention, shared expert, dense layers, embed and lm_head)
architecture: flint MoE, 40B total / ~2.5B active, 49 layers (2 dense + 47 MoE), 256 routed experts top-6 + 1 shared, 35 sliding-window (513) + 14 full-attention layers, vision-capable (engine_type vlm)

baseline.note: re-established in this pass on the corrected config (activation_fp16_enabled=false, enable_thinking=false, empty prefix cache). Matches the pre-correction baseline within noise, so it is trustworthy.

final_medians.note: 3-run measurement after one discarded warmup, on the applied final config. ttfc_ms is the median first *content* token across the three quality-guardrail prompts; flint always streams reasoning_content first, so TTFC is the user-visible latency, not TTFT.

rationale: Every knob that is actually wired up on flint was swept paired, and the honest answer is that none of them beat the corrected baseline. KV quantization is the clearest rejection: all three quantized arms lose 16-18% decode (114.94 -> 94.22-96.78 tps) and cost 5-11 ms of TTFT, because this model is memory-bandwidth-bound on a 2.5B-active MoE and dequantizing the KV cache on every step costs more than the bandwidth it saves. Context window is a genuine no-op: native 262144 and 32768 are within 1.7 ms TTFT and 0.35 tps at a 34-token prompt, at 16k, and at 20k, and resident memory is byte-identical (22.84 GB) either way, so there is no memory argument for capping it either. Native is kept because it is free and it accepts prompts that 32768 rejects outright (a ~41k-token prompt returns HTTP 400 context_length_exceeded at 32768). MTP, DFlash and spec-prefill are not knobs on this model at all - there is no draft head - so they are documented as no-ops rather than measured. Sampling does not affect throughput; both the card sampler and a temp-0.2 coding sampler produced correct code on all three guardrail prompts, so the card sampler is kept and force_sampling stays false, letting the model's own generation_config.json win. The thinking levers are the interesting negative result: reasoning_effort and thinking_budget_tokens are both accepted by the API and both do nothing on flint, and reasoning length swings 3.7k-8.9k characters run to run regardless. That variance, not any setting, is what dominates TTFC (3.8-14.8 s) and therefore the user-visible latency of a small coding task. The final config is the corrected baseline: it is the fastest decode point measured, it is on the Pareto front for TTFT, and every alternative was either slower or indistinguishable.
failure_modes: activation_fp16_enabled: true is a corruption switch on this model, not a speedup - the server reports activation_fp16_supported: false. The prior pass's apparent 26x speedup was garbage output that never entered the reasoning phase. Left false and never swept.

A saturated 185 GB prefix cache poisons cached prefixes and makes the model look corrupt. It was quarantined to ~/.omlx/cache-quarantine-1793275318 before this pass; ~/.omlx/cache was 4.5 MB at start and refilled normally.

With max_tokens 120-150 flint spends the entire budget on reasoning_content and returns content: '' with finish_reason: length. That is not corruption. Every quality check here streams with max_tokens >= 3000.

enable_thinking is a no-op: chat_template.jinja has no such switch. All thinking levers (reasoning_effort low..max, enable_thinking false, chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking false, thinking_budget_tokens 64..1024) produce statistically identical output.
thinking_budget_enabled/thinking_budget_tokens are accepted by PUT and echoed back but are not enforced on flint; reasoning length is unchanged within run-to-run variance.
A --context-pad of 30000 expands to ~41k tokens, which 32768 rejects with HTTP 400 context_length_exceeded. Pad sizes must be checked against the cap under test.
Changing a reload-requiring setting unloads the model; auto_unloaded does not reload it. POST /load and poll until loaded: true before measuring.
measure.py intermittently exits non-zero with no 'run 1:' line; retry up to 3x.
measurement_caveat: Absolute throughput drifts between runs, so no number here is comparable to a number from a different block. Every verdict is a paired comparison: interleaved A/B for non-reloading knobs (context, sampling), forward+backward ordering for the reload-requiring KV sweep. The baseline (251.0 ms / 114.6 tps) and the final (252.0 ms / 113.23 tps) are the same configuration measured at different times and differ by 1.2%, which is the scale of drift to expect.
